name: Joseph Cassano

summary.text: Joseph Cassano ran AIG Financial Products, the AIG unit whose credit default swap portfolio generated the collateral calls that preceded the federal rescue of AIG in September 2008. A House Oversight Committee memorandum in October 2008 said he had received more than $280 million over eight years and that AIG retained him as a consultant at $1 million a month after his departure. In May 2010 federal prosecutors told his lawyers that no criminal charges would be filed after a two-year investigation; an SEC civil inquiry was reported to be continuing at that time.

facts.claim: In May 2010 federal prosecutors informed lawyers for Cassano and Andrew Forster that no criminal charges would be filed after a roughly two-year investigation into whether AIG Financial Products officials misled investors and auditors about the value of its credit default swap portfolio.
facts.quote: Lawyers representing Joseph Cassano, who formerly ran AIG's Financial Products unit, and Andrew Forster, who worked for Cassano, said they were told by federal prosecutors late Friday that no criminal charges would be filed.

sources.title: Justice Dept. won't file charges in AIG case
DOJ drops criminal probe of AIG executive

facts.claim: At the time the criminal probe closed, an SEC investigation into AIG and its London-based Financial Products subsidiary was reported to be continuing.
facts.quote: A Securities and Exchange Commission probe into AIG and the dealings of its London-based Financial Products subsidiary is continuing and could lead to a civil securities fraud case.

sources.title: Justice Dept. won't file charges in AIG case

facts.claim: The House Oversight Committee under Henry Waxman stated in October 2008 that AIG was paying Cassano $1 million a month as a consultant after his departure and that he remained eligible for up to $34 million in unvested bonuses; reports said AIG stopped the retainer in October 2008 under congressional pressure.
facts.quote: Cassano received a $1 million monthly retainer from the company until AIG stopped the payments earlier this month under pressure from Congress.

facts.claim: Cassano's total compensation in the eight years through 2007 was about $280 million, a figure reported by Representative Henry Waxman in 2008 and later attributed to a Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission document; his pay peaked at $44.6 million in 2003.
facts.quote: The total in the eight years through 2007 was about $280 million, a figure previously reported by U.S. Rep. Henry Waxman, D-Calif.

facts.claim: In written testimony to the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission in 2010, Cassano defended AIG Financial Products' credit default swap book.

openQuestions: Site claim that Cassano 'received roughly $280 million over eight years': supported by the Waxman committee figure and a Business Insurance report citing an FCIC document.
Site claim that AIGFP 'wrote over $500 billion of credit protection' and generally did not post collateral: not tested in this file.
The SEC never announced charges against Cassano as far as the sources found show; whether the civil inquiry was formally closed was not confirmed.
The FCIC final report's own wording on Cassano was not retrieved.
